amanali-country-club.name: Amanali
amanali-country-club.note: Considered one of the 10 best courses in Mexico. Schmidt & Curley designed the layout on the banks of a lake in Tepeji del Río — zigzagging through canyons and cactus with panoramic lake views from most holes. Bermuda fairways, Bent Grass greens, 7,400 yards that would play closer to 8,200 at sea level once the altitude advantage is removed. A resort development surrounds the course, with the clubhouse designed by Legorreta Arquitectos. 50 minutes from Polanco — the best day-trip course in the CDMX corridor for golfers without a local membership.
amanali-country-club.standout: Canyon and lake routing — no two holes share the same terrain type. The back nine plays harder than the front.

bajamar-ocean-front-golf-resort.name: Bajamar Ocean Front Golf Resort
bajamar-ocean-front-golf-resort.access: Resort (open to the public by reservation)
bajamar-ocean-front-golf-resort.note: Twenty-seven holes on the Pacific north of Ensenada, Baja California: the Lagos, Vista and Oceano nines, the last one along the cliffs.

bosque-real-country-club.name: Bosque Real
bosque-real-country-club.access: Private: you play with a member. Confirmation needed
bosque-real-country-club.note: One of the longest courses in Mexico at 7,552 yards — and at altitude, every yard plays significantly easier than on the card thanks to the thinner air. Translated to sea level, this would be a brutal championship layout closer to 8,400 yards. Von Hagge's 18-hole design winds through mountain terrain with a river, canyons, ponds, and multiple lakes. Earned the LPGA MasterCard Classic from 2005 to 2009. Lorena Ochoa played here. Louise Friberg holds the women's course record at 65. A 9-hole executive course by Gary Nicklaus opened in 2008 alongside the championship layout. 15 km west of CDMX in Huixquilucan — 20 minutes from Santa Fe on a clear day. Some public booking available on weekdays with advance coordination.
bosque-real-country-club.standout: #18 — par 5, 624 yards from the tips. The longest hole on the course.

cabo-del-sol-golf-course.name: Cabo del Sol Golf Course
cabo-del-sol-golf-course.note: Tom Weiskopf desert-and-canyon course with Sea of Cortez views, renovated with six new Fry/Straka holes in 2023.

cabo-real-golf-course.name: Cabo Real Golf Course
cabo-real-golf-course.note: Robert Trent Jones II design with elevated tees and greens that climb from the sea toward the foothills, and panoramic ocean views.

chileno-bay-golf-club.name: Chileno Bay Golf Club
chileno-bay-golf-club.access: Private (members and guests of Chileno Bay Resort & Residences)
chileno-bay-golf-club.note: Tom Fazio's only Cabo design — built on graceful, flowing landforms intended to simulate rolling ocean waves. An ocean view from every hole. Back-to-back par 5s at holes 6 and 7. Two driveable short par 4s. The par-4 18th tumbles downhill to an infinity-edge green at 512 yards from the tips. Auberge Chileno Bay resort guests only.
chileno-bay-golf-club.standout: #18 — 512 yards downhill to an infinity-edge green.

club-campestre-san-jose.name: Club Campestre San José
club-campestre-san-jose.note: Best value on the corridor. Weaves through rugged desert arroyos with the Sierra de la Laguna mountains framing every shot. The truest sense of Baja's inland topography. Always described as the best value on the corridor — and consistently in top condition. Partner courses with Puerto Los Cabos and Cabo Real for combo packages. Fee includes practice balls, cart, water.
club-campestre-san-jose.standout: #7 — Demanding approach over a deep arroyo crossing.

club-de-golf-avandaro.name: Club de Golf Avándaro
club-de-golf-avandaro.note: The oldest resort course near Mexico City still in operation. Percy Clifford's 1959 design sits inside the Avandaro Golf & Spa Resort — 200 hectares of forested resort in Valle de Bravo, the lakeside town 90 minutes west of the capital. Flat, harmoniously set into pine forest, with water hazards, doglegs, and strategic bunkers that make it interesting across skill levels. The draw is not the design — it is the setting. Valle de Bravo is one of the most beautiful weekend escapes from Mexico City: pine trees, a lake, a colonial town center, and a pace of life the capital does not offer. Closed Mondays. Handicap certificate required.
club-de-golf-avandaro.standout: The forest setting — pine tree corridors and a mountain backdrop no other course near CDMX offers.

club-de-golf-chapultepec.name: Club de Golf Chapultepec
club-de-golf-chapultepec.access: Private: you play with a member. Estimate of $500 green fee + $100 member fee per person per round; confirmation needed
club-de-golf-chapultepec.note: The most historically important golf course in Mexico. Designed in 1921 by U.S. Open champion Willie Smith and completed by his brother Alex; redesigned by Percy Clifford in 1972. Mexican Open host 18 times, WGC-Mexico Championship 4 times (2017–2020), LIV Golf Mexico City in 2025 and 2026. At 7,800 feet above sea level, tight tree-lined fairways and undulating terrain make club selection a constant negotiation. The uphill trio of holes 15–17 is among the most demanding closing stretches in Mexican golf. Greens are small, very fast, severely sloped. Local knowledge is the differentiator. Member invitation only. No public tee times.
club-de-golf-chapultepec.standout: #17 — par 3, 167 yards. Water front and left. A miss left costs a number.

club-de-golf-malanquin.name: Club de Golf Malanquín
club-de-golf-malanquin.note: Tree-lined parkland course in San Miguel de Allende with kikuyu fairways, small lakes and streams.

club-de-golf-mexico.name: Club de Golf México
club-de-golf-mexico.access: Private: you play with a member. Estimate of $500 green fee + $100 member fee per person per round; confirmation needed
club-de-golf-mexico.note: The most prestigious private club in Mexico. Founded in 1947 in the Tlalpan corridor of southern CDMX, the course was designed by Percy Clifford — the architect responsible for shaping a generation of Mexican golf. Tight tree-lined fairways at 2,260 meters above sea level, with downtown Mexico City visible from multiple elevated tees. Hosted the World Cup of Golf in 1958 and 1968. Member invitation only; no public tee times. The dress code, the caddie program, and the clubhouse protocol set the standard the rest of the country still measures itself against.
club-de-golf-mexico.standout: Elevated tees with the CDMX skyline framing the fairway — the most photographed view in Mexican golf.

costa-palmas-golf-club.name: Costa Palmas Golf Club
costa-palmas-golf-club.note: Robert Trent Jones II links-style, walkable design on the East Cape; requires qualifying resort access.

diamante-dunes-course.name: Diamante Dunes Course
diamante-dunes-course.note: A true links experience framed by massive white sand dunes on the Pacific side of Cabo San Lucas. Walks and plays like a classic British course — with 340 days of sunshine. The standard by which all Cabo courses are measured.
diamante-dunes-course.standout: #17 — Par 3 with target semi-obscured by sand and scrub. The 590-yard par-5 18th plays to a shelf green perched 50 feet above the fairway.

diamante-el-cardonal.name: Diamante El Cardonal
diamante-el-cardonal.note: Tiger Woods' first solo design outside the United States. Wide, forgiving fairways through desert arroyos — highly playable for mixed-handicap groups, with panoramic Pacific views throughout. Host of the PGA Tour World Wide Technology Championship. Inspired by the classic West Coast courses Tiger grew up playing — Riviera, Bel-Air — with bold bunkers and wide fairway corridors.
diamante-el-cardonal.standout: #5 — The layout meanders through sand dunes on the outgoing holes; the back nine crisscrosses desert arroyos. Bold, flashed-face bunkers signpost the strategic options.

el-camaleon-mayakoba.name: El Camaleón Mayakoba
el-camaleon-mayakoba.access: Resort (visitor tee times; special rates for Mayakoba guests)
el-camaleon-mayakoba.note: The signature course of Caribbean golf in Mexico. Hosted the PGA Tour Mayakoba Golf Classic from 2007 to 2022 — the only PGA Tour event in Mexico during that run. Norman's routing weaves through three distinct ecosystems: mangrove, jungle, and beach, with a cenote crossing on the par-3 7th that is unlike any hole in the country. Limestone walls drop to the cenote below; the green floats above it. Access limited to guests of the Mayakoba resort hotels: Andaz, Banyan Tree, Fairmont, and Rosewood Mayakoba. Green fees include transportation.
el-camaleon-mayakoba.standout: #7 — Par 3 over a natural cenote with limestone walls and clear Caribbean water below the green. The most photographed hole in the Riviera Maya.

el-coral.name: Coral
el-coral.note: The 18-hole course with par-72 is perfectly incorporated into the natural surroundings of the high valley

el-cortes-golf-club.name: El Cortés Golf Club
el-cortes-golf-club.note: Gary Player Signature course near La Paz with Sea of Cortez views on 17 holes.

el-tamarindo-golf-course.name: El Tamarindo Golf Course
el-tamarindo-golf-course.note: David Fleming's nine holes at Four Seasons Resort Tamarindo on Jalisco's Costalegre, through tropical jungle and along a rocky Pacific coastline.

el-tigre-golf-club.name: El Tigre Golf Club
el-tigre-golf-club.note: Nine water features come into play on 12 holes. Challenge brief: "Create the most exciting championship golf course in Mexico." Von Hagge transformed a flat piece of land into a championship routing with molded elevation changes, 9 water features on 12 holes, and "beach bunkers" lurking at almost every turn. The stone archway at the entrance resembles a Mayan temple. The course finishes with two of its toughest holes. Champion Bermuda on greens, 419 Bermuda on fairways. Prevailing ocean winds — especially in late afternoon — add a variable the scorecard doesn't account for. Top 10 in Mexico 2008 (Golf Guide Magazine + Golf in Mexico Magazine).
el-tigre-golf-club.standout: #16 — par 4, 421 yards, long dogleg right. Approaches to a peninsula green. The hole that defines the course's water-and-accuracy character.

el-tinto-cancun-country-club.name: El Tinto
el-tinto-cancun-country-club.note: 18 holes, par 72, 6,791 yards — designed by Nick Price, who took advantage of the area's abundant environmental resources. Sits on the same property as Riviera Cancun Golf Club but is its own standalone layout. The vertical movement and natural rockwork make it one of the more distinctive inland rounds in the region. Open 7:00am to 4:00pm. Transportation available from Hotel Zone.
el-tinto-cancun-country-club.standout: The natural rock features integrated into the routing — limestone outcrops left in place as part of the course architecture rather than removed.

gran-coyote-golf-club.name: Gran Coyote
gran-coyote-golf-club.note: Formerly Grand Coral Golf Club. Nick Price laid heavy emphasis on minimal environmental impact — employing biologists and environmental consultants to determine how to minimize water consumption and protect native wildlife. The dense jungle comes into play along the fairways, requiring accuracy to navigate. Water hazards on several holes, strategically placed bunkers near the greens. Green fee includes shared cart with GPS, range balls, clubhouse facilities, and beach club access. 7 acres of lakes. Paspalum grass. 30 min from CUN.
gran-coyote-golf-club.standout: #5 signature hole · #7 at nearly 600 yards with angled green · closing four holes described as the hardest finish in the region.

higuera-golf-club.name: Higuera Golf Club
higuera-golf-club.note: The only course in this corridor bookable without a room key. 18 holes between virgin jungle and Pacific beach. 7 links-style holes along the coast, 8 through jungle, 2 signature holes directly on the beach. The #8 green is surrounded by water on three sides. Two snack bars on the course. Open 7:30am to 3:00pm. The honest entry point to the Punta Mita golf region. Direct booking at higueragolfclub.com.
higuera-golf-club.standout: #8 — peninsula green, water on three sides.

la-ceiba-golf-club.name: La Ceiba (Club de Golf de Yucatán)
la-ceiba-golf-club.note: Yucatán's first golf club, founded in 1970: a flat, walkable parkland course on the Mérida–Progreso highway, open to visitors every day. Green fee MXN 3,400 on weekdays and MXN 4,500 on weekends.

madeiras-country-club.name: Madeiras
madeiras-country-club.note: Wooded parkland course in Cuautitlán Izcalli, north of Mexico City, restored and known for its rolling, soft greens; access must be confirmed in advance.

mandarina-golf-club.name: Mandarina Golf Club
mandarina-golf-club.access: Semi-private (residents, One&Only guests and limited outside play)
mandarina-golf-club.note: Not a full 18. Nine par 3s, each with a name and a concept: The Redan, The Devil's Hole, The Queen, The Theater, The Bell. Plus one challenge hole — The Kraken — a near-island green with a pot bunker as the only escape. Norman: "El campo de Mandarina no tendrá parangón." ("Mandarina will have no equal.") Fee includes two rounds of 10 holes, cart with GPS, unlimited practice, and all food and beverages. No membership required. Transportation to the property needed from outside the Mandarina community.
mandarina-golf-club.standout: The Theater — Norman described it as one of the best medium-distance par 3s in the world.

moon-palace-golf-course.name: Moon Palace Golf Course
moon-palace-golf-course.note: The first Jack Nicklaus-designed golf course in Cancun. 27 holes offering almost 11,000 yards of play across three combination 18-hole layouts: Dunes & Jungle, Jungle & Lakes, and Lakes & Dunes. All-inclusive format: golf carts with GPS, air-conditioned snack bar, pro shop, and full-service restaurant. Tee times from 6:00am. All-inclusive guests can access golf for cart fee only ($38 first round, $19 subsequent) — the strongest all-inclusive value play on the corridor for golfers who plan 3+ rounds.
moon-palace-golf-course.standout: Lakes nine — the toughest of the three. Native wetlands, strategically placed bunkers, and jungle corridors create a significantly harder test than the scorecard suggests.

nauka-golf-club.name: Nauka Golf Club
nauka-golf-club.access: Private (limited access for Siari Ritz-Carlton Reserve guests)
nauka-golf-club.note: 920 acres. 400 memberships. One Tom Fazio course. Set against tropical jungle overlooking the Pacific. Undulating greens, challenging elevations, natural bunkering. A 9-hole short course runs alongside the championship layout for members of all levels. The community: 197-foot infinity pool, fresh seafood, firepits, a tequila room, a marina and yacht club, a wellness village, a beach racquet club. Siari, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve: 91 suites, 34 residences, five restaurants. No public access. No day-pass.
nauka-golf-club.standout: Four ecosystems in 18 holes — jungle, cliff, mangrove, beach. No two consecutive holes share a view.

oleada-golf-links.name: Oleada Golf Links
oleada-golf-links.access: Resort community (limited public play at opening; expected to go private)
oleada-golf-links.note: Pacific-side round in Los Cabos, subject to outside-player availability.

palma-real-golf-club.name: Palma Real Golf Club
palma-real-golf-club.note: Robert Trent Jones Jr. course in Ixtapa's hotel zone on the Pacific coast of Guerrero, with broad fairways, natural lakes with resident crocodiles and stands of coconut palms.

palmilla-golf-club.name: Palmilla Golf Club
palmilla-golf-club.access: Resort (One&Only Palmilla guests; the Arroyo nine stays open during the 2026 renovation)
palmilla-golf-club.note: The course that started the modern Tourist Corridor in 1992. Three interchangeable nines (Mountain, Arroyo, Ocean) — the first Jack Nicklaus Signature Design in Latin America. The Ocean nine, added in 1997, features a 600-foot elevation drop from tee to green. Outside play season- and time-dependent; preferred rates for One&Only Palmilla guests.
palmilla-golf-club.standout: Ocean #3 — Par 4 dropping 150 feet to a beachfront green steps from the crashing Sea of Cortez. The most photographed hole at Palmilla.

pga-riviera-maya-championship-course.name: PGA Riviera Maya
pga-riviera-maya-championship-course.note: During RTJ Jr.'s first week designing this course, he came armed with only a machete, his feet, and x-ray vision. The 290 acres were so dense with jungle he needed to design with the soles of his feet to know where to cut. 27 holes cut deep into a limestone quarry, with fairways emerging from the natural contours of a dense jungle combined with mangroves. Natural water, rock, cenotes, and native jungle are integral design elements. First PGA of America partner destination in Latin America (2019). Won Best Golf Course in Mexico at the 2024 World Golf Awards. Host of Mexico's first Korn Ferry Tour event in 2025. 90 min from CUN.
pga-riviera-maya-championship-course.standout: Cenotes integrated into the course as architectural features — not water hazards to avoid but genuine design elements that make this the most technically distinctive round in the region.

playa-mujeres-golf-club.name: Playa Mujeres Golf Club
playa-mujeres-golf-club.note: Located within 930 acres of the Playa Mujeres Resort, ideally situated between the Caribbean Sea and the Chachmuchuc Lagoon, with jungle vegetation that narrows the fairways at several points. Daily trade winds add strategic challenge. A nine-hole short course completed in 2024 by Greg Norman Golf Course Design joins the championship layout — 27 holes total. Green fees include round-trip hotel transportation. Paspalum SeaDwarf grass. 20 minutes north of CUN.
playa-mujeres-golf-club.standout: Caribbean and lagoon views from multiple holes — the ocean glimpses on the back nine are the most dramatic on the corridor north of Mayakoba.

puerto-cancun-golf-club.name: Puerto Cancún Golf Club
puerto-cancun-golf-club.note: Situated between Cancun's hotel zone and the downtown area. Tom Weiskopf's design allows the natural beauty of the tropical landscape to be the star. Several holes play along the shoreline and Marina — almost every hole offers views of the Caribbean. Stretches to just over 7,200 yards from the back tees. The 18th green is situated on an island in Puerto Cancun's major canal. The par-4 14th plays parallel to the Caribbean shoreline for more than 400 yards. Golf Advisor Top 10 in Mexico every year 2020–2024. Toptracer at the driving range.
puerto-cancun-golf-club.standout: #18 — Island green in Puerto Cancun's main canal. The most dramatic closing hole in Cancun proper.

puerto-los-cabos-golf-club.name: Puerto Los Cabos Golf Club
puerto-los-cabos-golf-club.note: Now a 27-hole facility with three 18-hole combinations. Nicklaus returned in 2017 to build a second nine, opened in 2018. Norman's course has 400+ feet of elevation change. The only Nicklaus + Norman collaboration in Mexico. Fee includes practice balls, cart, food + beverages.
puerto-los-cabos-golf-club.standout: #18 — Norman's finishing hole running parallel to the marina and coastline.

punta-mita-bahia.name: Punta Mita Bahía
punta-mita-bahia.access: Private (owners; Four Seasons and St. Regis guests)
punta-mita-bahia.note: Same peninsula. Caddie included. More forgiving off the tee. Bahia moves through tropical jungle before finding the ocean on the closing holes. The last shot of the round is a forced carry over water — the only ocean-carry par 5 in Mexico. You make the decision before you take the club back. Resort access only — Four Seasons, St. Regis, private residences.
punta-mita-bahia.standout: #18 — commit or lay up. The round ends with a choice.

punta-mita-pacifico.name: Punta Mita Pacífico
punta-mita-pacifico.access: Private (owners; Four Seasons and St. Regis guests)
punta-mita-pacifico.note: 380 acres of peninsula. Eight holes on the Pacific. The course features an optional island green — the Tail of the Whale (hole 3B) — reached across a natural stone causeway at low tide. It is the only natural island green in golf. Ask the pro shop the night before for the tide window. If your tee time falls inside it, go. If not, play 3A. The round holds either way. Caddie included from the shuttle to the final putt. Resort access only — Four Seasons, St. Regis, private residences.
punta-mita-pacifico.standout: 3B — nothing else like it in golf.

quivira-golf-club.name: Quivira Golf Club
quivira-golf-club.note: The crown jewel of the corridor. Quivira plays along the Pacific cliffs above Cabo San Lucas — every hole delivers an ocean view, climbing out of desert canyons to finish with one of the most photographed closing stretches in North America. Rates include cart, practice facility, and all food and refreshments at four comfort stations. Accessible to guests of Pueblo Bonito Oceanfront Resorts: Pacifica · Sunset Beach · Rosé · Los Cabos.
quivira-golf-club.standout: #13 — Par 3 returning to the cliffs, 150 feet above the Pacific. The most photographed hole on the course. The par-4 fifth climbs 275 feet up the mountain — one of the most dramatic tee shots in Mexico.

rancho-avandaro-golf-club.name: Rancho Avándaro
rancho-avandaro-golf-club.access: Semi-private (gated residential community; access to be confirmed)
rancho-avandaro-golf-club.note: Mountain course routed through pines inside the Rancho Avándaro residential community, with holes that climb, drop and play blind; a different course from Club de Golf Avándaro.

riviera-cancun-golf-resorts.name: Riviera Cancún Golf & Resorts
riviera-cancun-golf-resorts.note: A Jack Nicklaus design at 7,060 yards, carved using the terrain's natural contours, with ocean views throughout. Located near Cancun airport on the same property as El Tinto — but a separate, standalone Nicklaus championship layout. The pre-flight round on the corridor. Open 7:00am to 4:00pm. Transportation available from Hotel Zone.
riviera-cancun-golf-resorts.standout: #14 and #15 — the Nicklaus signature stretch. Two strategic risk-reward holes back-to-back along the natural ridgeline.

solmar-golf-links.name: Solmar Golf Links
solmar-golf-links.note: A genuine links course with revetted pot bunkers identical to British seaside links — the only ones in Mexico. Three ecosystems: Pacific dunes, cactus forest, coastal finish. Several holes play directly toward the beach. Greg Norman's least-disturbance design approach preserved the natural contours entirely. And yes — Troy was filmed on these cliffs. Solmar Group hotel guests preferred rates; rates include cart, water, practice facility, and two on-course comfort stations.
solmar-golf-links.standout: Pacific stretch — links holes hanging directly over the Pacific Ocean.

tpc-danzante-bay.name: TPC Danzante Bay
tpc-danzante-bay.note: Rees Jones design that descends from canyons to the Sea of Cortez; the signature 17th is a cliffside par 3.

twin-dolphin-golf-club.name: Twin Dolphin Golf Club
twin-dolphin-golf-club.note: Built on the historic grounds of the original Twin Dolphin Hotel. Incredible elevation changes and tournament-level greens — the Sea of Cortez visible from almost every tee. Includes practice facilities + two on-course comfort stations. Accessible to guests of Montage Los Cabos (122-room hotel) and Montage Residences.
twin-dolphin-golf-club.standout: Perched 180 meters above sea level on a broad plateau bisected by three major arroyos. Sea of Cortes visible from every hole. The par-3 third plays across a jagged canyon — one of the most dramatic par 3s on the corridor.

ventanas-de-san-miguel.name: Ventanas de San Miguel
ventanas-de-san-miguel.note: Nick Faldo design above San Miguel de Allende with dramatic elevation change and long championship holes.

vidanta-nayar-course.name: Nayar Course
vidanta-nayar-course.access: Resort (open to the public by reservation; caddie required)
vidanta-nayar-course.note: Jack Nicklaus par-70 championship course with seven lakes, 49 bunkers and ocean wind; caddie service is part of the experience.

vidanta-puerto-penasco-nicklaus-course.name: Vidanta Puerto Peñasco Nicklaus Course
vidanta-puerto-penasco-nicklaus-course.design: Jack Nicklaus and Jack Nicklaus II
vidanta-puerto-penasco-nicklaus-course.access: Resort (open to the public by reservation)
vidanta-puerto-penasco-nicklaus-course.note: Jack Nicklaus and Jack Nicklaus II design at Vidanta Puerto Peñasco, Sonora, with the Sea of Cortez on three sides, 87 bunkers and two lakes.

vidanta-the-lakes-course.name: The Lakes Course
vidanta-the-lakes-course.access: Resort (open to the public and guests by reservation; lit for night play)
vidanta-the-lakes-course.note: Ten-hole par-3 executive course with carries over lakes and bunkers, lit for night play; a round takes about two hours.

vidanta-vallarta-course.name: Vidanta Vallarta Course
vidanta-vallarta-course.access: Resort (Vidanta tee times subject to availability)
vidanta-vallarta-course.note: The only active PGA Tour venue in Puerto Vallarta. Designed by Greg Norman. Host of the Mexico Open at VidantaWorld since 2022 — an official PGA Tour event awarding 500 FedEx Cup points to the winner. Jon Rahm won in 2022, Tony Finau in 2023, Jake Knapp in 2024. The 2026 event moves to October 29–November 1 with a $6 million purse. "Renovation of the Year" by Golf Inc. magazine in 2022. Wall-to-wall paspalum, layout winds along the Ameca River with views of the Sierra Madre. 15 lakes. 49 bunkers. The longest golf cart suspension bridge in the world — 560 feet spanning the Ameca River — connects the clubhouse to the course. Hole 10 was ranked the toughest on the 2023 PGA Tour. Open to Vidanta resort guests and public with advance booking. Caddies mandatory and paid in cash at the course (Single $28 · 2-some $45 · 3-some $56 · 4-some $67).
vidanta-vallarta-course.standout: #7 — driveable par 4 at 297 yards. Water left, bunkers right. One of the most discussed risk-reward holes on the Mexico Open schedule.

vista-vallarta-nicklaus-course.name: Vista Vallarta Nicklaus Course
vista-vallarta-nicklaus-course.note: The most prestigious public course in the Puerto Vallarta corridor. Perched at the property's highest elevation — breathtaking views of Puerto Vallarta, the Marina, and Banderas Bay from nearly every tee box. Grassy hillsides, dense forests of palm and giant ficus trees, natural creeks and arroyos. True to Nicklaus style: wildly undulating greens balanced by generous driving areas. Host of the 2002 WGC-World Cup. Course record: 62, Phil Mickelson. Rating: 73.8 · Slope: 144. 15 min from PVR.
vista-vallarta-nicklaus-course.standout: #3 — par 5, 550 yards. Three strong shots required. Elevation rises with every swing. The most demanding hole on the Banderas Bay corridor.

vista-vallarta-weiskopf-course.name: Vista Vallarta Weiskopf Course
vista-vallarta-weiskopf-course.note: The more accessible side of Vista Vallarta's double routing. Built on the property's lower west end — dense jungle, deep ravines, swift creeks. A dramatically different landscape from the Nicklaus course despite sharing the same clubhouse. Fewer blind shots and more receptive greens make it the preferred round for mixed-handicap groups. Wide fairways, natural hazards, Weiskopf's signature finesse on the par 3s. Rating: 74.7 (gold) · Slope: 138.
vista-vallarta-weiskopf-course.standout: #15 — uphill par 3 over a ravine. Multi-tiered green, bunkers on all sides. Concentration required from the tee.
